about: The moth's foils, gantry and wand (docs/moth-4). Game frame: x forward from the hull's middle, y to starboard, z up from the design waterline (at rest, sailor aboard), metres. Sizes are the size card's (typical for today's boats: a 'big' main foil of about 1.0 m and 0.12 m^2, an elevator of about 0.7 m); shapes are plain NACA four-digit sections, nothing copied from any builder's foil.

strut.note: the main foil's vertical strut (the daggerboard): through a case in the hull (class rule 6.3.3: it leaves the hull below the waterline), 0.6 m aft of the mast step (Milestone A moved it from x 0.30: the camera-matched flying photo fits best with it at 0.0 to 0.1, and four of six blind reviewers saw it too far forward); its foot 1.05 m below the hull's lowest point

main_foil.note: a T at the strut's foot, straight quarter-chord line, taper 0.55; the flap (MOTH_Flap) is the aft 30% of the inner 82% of the span, drawn at 0 deg (the game turns it about the FlapHinge socket's axis) Milestone B: span 1.0 to 1.1 m, chords 0.155/0.085 to 0.145/0.07 (about the same area, a higher aspect ratio): reviewers in rounds 1 and 3 read the foils as broad plates beside the photos' slender blades with spans close to the strut's length

pod.note: the junction's fairing: a slim torpedo that carries the flap's pushrod bellcrank

gantry.note: two carbon tubes from the transom's corners converging to the rudder's stock behind the hull (class rule 6.1.2: removable, and inside the 500 mm allowance of 6.1.5) Milestone B: 0.45 to 0.5 m (all six reviewers read it as short; the photos' reach about 17% of the hull's length behind the transom) and a second pair of tubes from the transom's lower corners, so the gantry reads as the triangulated truss the photos show (two reviewers read it as short and a single bar) ; 0.5 m is rule 6.1.5's allowance, so no further

rudder.note: a straight vertical blade hung on the gantry; its foot at the same depth as the main foil's

elevator.note: the T at the rudder's foot; the twist grip turns the whole elevator (or the rudder blade's rake) a few degrees, drawn at 0 (the game turns it about ElevatorPivot) Milestone B: span 0.72 to 0.8 m, chords 0.11/0.07 to 0.10/0.062, the same area, slimmer, as the main foil

wand.note: hinged on a short bow fitting right at the stem (the flying photo shows the pivot there; Milestone A moved it back from 0.12 m ahead so the tip stays inside the class rule 6.1.5 allowance of 0.5 m past the hull); drawn in the flying pose, its paddle on the water 0.45 m under the hull's lowest point (the game swings it about WandPivot from the wave height under its tip) Milestone B: drawn trailing aft of its pivot (about 6 deg off vertical at flying height: the camera-matched flying photo puts its paddle only about 0.07 m behind the pivot). The lower bow brought the pivot down, so the wand is 0.88 m (the drop from the pivot to the water 0.45 m under the hull is 0.87 m), and its fitting stands 0.1 m ahead of the stem so the trailing wand clears the plumb bow (at 0.03 m it ran through the stem) instead of raking forward: all nine reviewers over Milestones A and B saw the real wands hang nearly upright and trail slightly aft, the drag on the paddle pushing it back against its shock cord
